equivalent.old: skipping = nl < 0                  # the rest of this line is dropped as it arrives
equivalent.proof: The line is reached only when held + len(piece) > max_line. If nl == 0 then start == 0 (nl >= start) so piece == b'' and the test is held > max_line. Invariant 0 <= held <= max_line (held is reset to 0 or grows only when held + len(piece) <= max_line), and every caller uses max_line = MAX_LINE >= 0 (no other max_line in src/). So nl == 0 never reaches this line, and for nl != 0 'nl < 0' == 'nl <= 0'. Fuzz: 20,000 random multi-member streams, max_line 0..8, outputs identical (MP-C3b).

equivalent.old: raw_host = netloc.rsplit(":", 1)[0] if ":" in netloc and not netloc.endswith("]") else netloc
equivalent.proof: The two differ only when ':' is in netloc AND netloc ends with ']'. p.port was already read (any non-numeric port raised -> urls_invalid), and urlsplit (CPython 3.13.18) refuses any text before '[' in the host part, so netloc (after the userinfo) starts with '['. Then both the original raw_host (netloc) and the mutant's (netloc up to its last ':') start with '[', which no _LABEL accepts: both return (None, 'urls_invalid'). Exhaustive check: 813,615 URLs built from bracket/colon/at/IPv6/IPvFuture/percent fragments (length 1..5), normalise identical. Note: on a CPython without the before-'[' check, test_mp_link_edges.py::test_B_MP_22_bracketed_authority_after_a_colon_is_invalid_not_the_prefix_host kills it.
